I will keep to the cropping pattern I know best here in Quzhou County: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. I am 73, so I will not chase complicated crops that need more labor, more market watching, or more risk. Wheat and maize are what I understand, the machines can handle them, the buyers are easy to find, and the income is steady enough. If I try vegetables, cotton, or too many different crops, I will have to spend more time in the field and worry more about pests, prices, and selling. I do not want that.

So for this year, I will keep my whole field in the wheat-maize rotation. The wheat is already the backbone of the year, and after wheat harvest I will plant summer maize right away so the land does not sit empty. I will use better seed, but not anything fancy that is hard to manage. I will put fertilizer at a moderate level because I want stable yield, not waste. I will irrigate when the crop really needs it, especially for wheat at the key stages and for maize after sowing and around jointing or tasseling if the weather is dry. I will spray only as needed for the common diseases, insects, and weeds, because too much spraying costs money and is hard on me physically. For tillage, I will keep it simple: rotary tillage for wheat, then no-tillage maize after wheat harvest to save labor and catch the season on time.
